preamble: You probably think of notifications as something you switch on or off once, somewhere in your account. In Docs they work the other way round: each document carries its own rules about when it should email you. So what you're really looking for isn't a global preference — it's a setting that belongs to this document, about the people working in it alongside you.
generalization: Notification settings sit with the document, not with your account, because the thing being described is this document's activity — its comments, its edits, its collaborators. That's also why the Tools menu is the right place to look: File is about the document as an object, Format is about the text, and Tools is about the things Docs does around your writing — checking it, counting it, watching it, and telling you when someone else touches it.

steps.intent: Nothing you're about to change affects a single word on the page. You're setting a rule about when Docs should reach out to you about other people's activity here. That kind of thing — the work Docs does around your writing rather than to it — is gathered under Tools.
hints: You're not editing text and you're not editing the file. You're configuring something Docs does on your behalf while you work.
In the menu bar along the top, between Format and Extensions.

wrongHints.File: A reasonable guess — File holds settings about the document as an object, like sharing and page setup. But notifications aren't a property of the file; they're about activity happening inside it while you're away.
wrongHints.Edit: Edit acts on the content you've selected. Notifications never touch content.
wrongHints.Help: Help explains how Docs works. You're not looking for an explanation, you're looking for a switch that belongs to this document.

steps.intent: Open Notification settings. What opens is a short list of choices about comments and edits — who has to be involved before Docs emails you. Note that it applies to this document alone, which is why it lives here and not in a global preferences screen.
hints: Most of this menu is about inspecting the document — spelling, word count, suggested edits. You want the one item that's about being told something later.
Partway down the Tools menu, in the group below the review and counting tools.

wrongHints.Preferences: Preferences sounds exactly right, but it's about how the editor behaves as you type — autocorrect, substitutions — and it applies everywhere, not to this document.
